Let $R$ be a commutative ring ([[def-commutative-ring]]). An **$R$-algebra** is a unital ring $A$ together with a unital ring homomorphism

$$\eta_A:R\longrightarrow A$$

([[def-ring-homomorphism]]) whose image is central: $\eta_A(r)a=a\eta_A(r)$ for every $r\in R$ and $a\in A$. The induced scalar action is $ra:=\eta_A(r)a$, making $A$ an $R$-module and multiplication $A\times A\to A$ bilinear.

An **$R$-algebra homomorphism** $f:A\to B$ is a unital ring homomorphism satisfying $f\circ\eta_A=\eta_B$. Such a map is automatically $R$-linear. An $R$-algebra is **commutative** when its underlying ring is commutative.

Fix $r,n\ge1$ and use the independent units $Q,u_1,\ldots,u_r$ of [[def-hh-multiplicative-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]. An **$r$-multipartition** of $n$ is a tuple $\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(r)})$ of ordinary partitions whose total number of boxes is $n$. Its boxes are triples $(c,a,b)$ with $1\le c\le r$, $a\ge1$, and $1\le b\le\lambda^{(c)}_a$. Order the boxes within component $c$ by the transitive closure of $(c,a,b)<(c,a,b+1)$ and $(c,a,b)<(c,a+1,b)$; boxes in different components are incomparable.

A **standard multitableau** $t$ of shape $\lambda$ is a bijective filling of the boxes by $1,\ldots,n$ that increases along every row and column. Equivalently, it is a linear extension of this finite box poset. Write $\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)$ for the set of such fillings and

$$ \operatorname{res}_t(i)=u_cQ^{b-a}\quad\text{if entry }i\text{ occupies }(c,a,b). $$

The **generic content field** is $K=\mathbb Q(Q,u_1,\ldots,u_r)$, the fraction field of $R$. The contents of distinct addable boxes of any multipartition are distinct in $K$. If two boxes in one component have the same content, they lie on one diagonal; the right and lower boxes immediately between them are distinct required predecessors of the southeast box. Consequently, for three consecutive labels $i,i+1,i+2$ in a standard multitableau, the first and third contents cannot agree. In particular every pair of contents among three consecutive labels is distinct in $K$. If two boxes in one component have content exponents differing by $1$, then they are comparable in the box order, so interchanging adjacent labels in a standard multitableau never gives a content ratio $Q$ or $Q^{-1}$.

derivations.claim: The dominance inequalities are reflexive and transitive. If they hold in both directions, all displayed cumulative sums are equal; subtracting successive row cutoffs and then successive component prefixes recovers every row length in every component, so $\lambda=\mu$. Thus $\unrhd$ is a partial order. The tableau $t^\lambda$ is standard: its entries increase left to right by construction, and every box in an earlier row or earlier component is filled before every box in a later row or component, so each column also increases top to bottom.

Fix $\lambda$. If $\mu>\lambda$, the cell axiom applied to $C^\mu_{u,v}a$ puts it in the span of the shape-$\mu$ basis elements plus $A^{>\mu}$. Every shape in that expression is strictly above $\lambda$ by transitivity; hence $A^{>\lambda}$ is a right ideal. Since $*$ preserves each shape and $A^{>\lambda}$, $a x=(x^*a^*)^*$ lies in $A^{>\lambda}$ whenever $x$ does, so it is also a left ideal. The same argument with $\mu\ge\lambda$ proves that $A^{\ge\lambda}$ is a two-sided ideal.

The given basis of $A^{\ge\lambda}$ is the disjoint union of the shape-$\lambda$ basis and the basis of $A^{>\lambda}$. Linear independence therefore makes the classes of $C^\lambda_{s,t}$ a basis of the quotient $A^{\ge\lambda}/A^{>\lambda}$. No choice is needed because the poset and every indexing set are finite.

Fix integers $r,n\ge1$. Put $R=\mathbb Z[Q^{\pm1},u_1^{\pm1},\ldots,u_r^{\pm1}]$ and $p(X)=\prod_{a=1}^r(X-u_a)$. Let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{aff}}$ be the unital associative $R$-algebra on generators $T_1,\ldots,T_{n-1}$ and $X_1^{\pm1},\ldots,X_n^{\pm1}$, with central $R$-action, subject to

$$ (T_i-Q)(T_i+1)=0,\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1},\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\ (|i-j|>1), $$

$$ X_jX_k=X_kX_j,\qquad T_iX_j=X_jT_i\ (j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad T_iX_iT_i=QX_{i+1}. $$

Here the braid relation is imposed for $1\le i<n-1$ and the distant commutation relation for $1\le i,j<n$. Define the **multiplicative cyclotomic Hecke algebra of level $r$ and rank $n$** by

$$ H_{r,n}=\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{aff}}/(p(X_1)), $$

where $(p(X_1))$ denotes the two-sided ideal it generates. The unit $Q$ and the quadratic relation make every $T_i$ invertible, with $T_i^{-1}=Q^{-1}(T_i-(Q-1))$. The cyclotomic relation also gives the polynomial inverse

$$ X_1^{-1}=(-1)^{r+1}(u_1\cdots u_r)^{-1}\bigl(X_1^{r-1}-e_1X_1^{r-2}+\cdots+(-1)^{r-1}e_{r-1}\bigr), $$

where $e_k$ is the $k$th elementary symmetric polynomial in $u_1,\ldots,u_r$. The presentation already includes inverse generators; this formula records that the quotient does not require a separate inverse parameter. For $i\ge1$, write $X_{i+1}=Q^{-1}T_iX_iT_i$ when using the recursion determined by the affine relation.

This is the multiplicative presentation. It is not the additive degenerate cyclotomic presentation obtained after setting a parameter equal to $1$ and changing generators.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $S$ a set. There is a unital associative $R$-algebra $R\langle S\rangle$, the **free associative $R$-algebra on $S$**, whose underlying $R$-module is free on the set of finite words in $S$ (including the empty word), with product given on words by concatenation and extended $R$-bilinearly.

1. **Universal property.** For every $R$-algebra $A$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) and every map $S\to A$ there is a unique unital $R$-algebra homomorphism $R\langle S\rangle\to A$ extending it. When $R=k$ is a field and $S$ indexes a basis of a vector space $V$, $R\langle S\rangle$ reproduces the published tensor algebra $T(V)$ ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]).
2. **Two-sided ideal description.** For $E\subseteq R\langle S\rangle$ the two-sided ideal $(E)$ ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) is the set of finite sums $\sum_sa_se_sb_s$ with $a_s,b_s\in R\langle S\rangle$ and $e_s\in E$.
3. **Quotient universal property.** If $\varphi:R\langle S\rangle\to A$ is an $R$-algebra homomorphism killing $E$, then $\varphi$ factors uniquely through the quotient $R\langle S\rangle/(E)$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]); the quotient is the presented $R$-algebra with generators $S$ and relations $E$.

In $H_{r,n}$ define

$$ L_1=X_1,\qquad L_i=Q^{1-i}T_{i-1}\cdots T_1X_1T_1\cdots T_{i-1}\quad(2\le i\le n). $$

Then $L_i=X_i$ for every $i$, so the $L_i$ commute and are units. For $1\le i<n$ they satisfy

$$ T_iL_iT_i=QL_{i+1},\qquad T_iL_i=L_{i+1}T_i-(Q-1)L_{i+1},\qquad T_iL_{i+1}=L_iT_i+(Q-1)L_{i+1}, $$

and $T_iL_j=L_jT_i$ when $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$. More generally, for every polynomial $f\in R[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$,

$$ T_if(L_1,\ldots,L_n)=f(s_iL_1,\ldots,s_iL_n)T_i-(Q-1)L_{i+1}\frac{f(L_1,\ldots,L_n)-f(s_iL_1,\ldots,s_iL_n)}{L_i-L_{i+1}}, $$

where $s_i$ interchanges the $i$th and $(i+1)$st variables and the displayed divided difference is a polynomial. In particular the cyclotomic relation transports as

$$ T_ip(L_i)=p(L_{i+1})T_i-(Q-1)L_{i+1}\frac{p(L_i)-p(L_{i+1})}{L_i-L_{i+1}}. $$

When $p(L_i)=0$, this gives $p(L_{i+1})T_i=(Q-1)L_{i+1}(p(L_i)-p(L_{i+1}))/(L_i-L_{i+1})$; the cyclotomic quotient guarantees this only for $i=1$. It does **not** impose $p(L_i)=0$ for every $i$.

derivations.claim: On the free associative algebra define $*$ by $r^*=r$ for $r\in R$, $T_i^*=T_i$, $X_j^*=X_j$, $(X_j^{-1})^*=X_j^{-1}$, and $(ab)^*=b^*a^*$, extending $R$-linearly. Word reversal is an involutive anti-automorphism, so this defines an involutive anti-automorphism of the free algebra.

The quadratic relation is a polynomial in one fixed generator and is fixed by reversal. Each braid word in the $T_i$ is palindromic, each distant commutation relation reverses to the same equality with sides exchanged, each relation $X_jX_k=X_kX_j$ and $T_iX_j=X_jT_i$ reverses to its equivalent reversed equality, and $T_iX_iT_i=QX_{i+1}$ is fixed because its left word is palindromic and $Q$ is central. The inverse relations reverse to the other inverse equations, and the cyclotomic relation $p(X_1)=0$ is fixed because it is a polynomial in $X_1$. Thus reversal sends every defining relator into the defining ideal. As the ideal is two-sided, it is preserved under reversal, so $*$ descends to an involutive anti-automorphism of $H_{r,n}$.

The quotient is generated by the displayed letters and $R$, so any anti-homomorphism fixing them is unique. By [F3], $L_j=X_j$, hence $L_j^*=L_j$. On words in the finite generators $T_i$, reversal sends a reduced word for $w$ to the reversed reduced word for $w^{-1}$; therefore $T_w^*=T_{w^{-1}}$, as for the finite reversal anti-involution.

Let $(S,m)$, $W$, $\ell$ be as in [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]; let $R$, $v_s$, $H$, $T_s$ be as in [[def-hh-universal-coxeter-hecke-parameters-and-presentation]]; let $T_w$ for $w\in W$ and the spanning statement be as in [[lem-hh-reduced-word-independence-and-length-multiplication]]; and let $E$, $P_s$, $Q_s$ and $P_w$ be as in [[lem-hh-commuting-left-right-hecke-length-operators]].

1. **The length-operator representation.** There is a unique unital $R$-algebra homomorphism $\rho:H\to\operatorname{End}_R(E)$ with $\rho(T_s)=P_s$ for all $s\in S$; it satisfies $\rho(T_w)=P_w$ and $\rho(T_w)(e_1)=e_w$ for all $w\in W$.
2. **Standard basis.** $\{T_w:w\in W\}$ is an $R$-basis of $H$: it spans by [[lem-hh-reduced-word-independence-and-length-multiplication]] and is $R$-linearly independent. Hence $H$ is free as an $R$-module and every element of $H$ has a unique expansion $\sum_wa_wT_w$ with $a_w\in R$ and all but finitely many $a_w$ zero.
3. **Faithfulness.** $\rho$ is injective.
4. **Base change.** For every commutative ring $R'$ and every ring homomorphism $\varphi:R\to R'$, the scalar extension $R'\otimes_RH$ is, as an $R'$-algebra, canonically isomorphic to the quotient of the free associative $R'$-algebra on $(T_s)_{s\in S}$ by the two-sided ideal generated by the images under $\varphi$ of the relations (Q) and (B) of [[def-hh-universal-coxeter-hecke-parameters-and-presentation]], and it is free as an $R'$-module with basis $(1\otimes T_w)_{w\in W}$. No flatness or freeness of $R'$ over $R$ is assumed, and no torsion-freeness or semisimplicity of $H$ or of its specialisations is claimed.

Let $(S,m)$ be a finite Coxeter matrix with presented group $W$, length $\ell$ and geometric representation $\sigma:W\to\mathrm{GL}_K(E)$ as in [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]], [[def-hh-geometric-coxeter-representation-and-roots]] and [[lem-hh-dihedral-root-recurrence-and-root-sign]], and let $J\subseteq S$.

1. **Support and reduction.** For every $w\in W$ the set $S(w)$ of letters occurring in a reduced expression of $w$ is independent of the reduced expression, and every word in $S$ representing $w$ can be transformed into a reduced expression by repeatedly deleting two letters (Tits reduction, using only letters already present). Consequently
$$W_J=\langle J\rangle=\{w\in W:S(w)\subseteq J\}.$$
2. **Intrinsic parabolic presentation.** Let $W_J^\ast$ be the group presented by the restricted Coxeter matrix $(J,m|_J)$ in the sense of [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]. The canonical homomorphism $W_J^\ast\to W_J$, $s\mapsto s$, is an isomorphism. Hence $(W_J,J)$ is a Coxeter system, its intrinsic length function $\ell_J$ agrees with the ambient length $\ell$ on $W_J$, and $W_J\cap S=J$.
3. **Minimal coset representatives.** Every right coset $W_J a:=\{ua:u\in W_J\}$ ($a\in W$, [[def-coset]]) has a unique element $d$ of minimal length; it is characterized by $\ell(sd)>\ell(d)$ for all $s\in J$, and it satisfies
$$\ell(ud)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)\qquad\text{for all }u\in W_J .$$
Equivalently, every $w\in W$ has a unique factorization $w=u\,d$ with $u\in W_J$ and $d$ the minimal representative of the right coset $W_J d$, and then $\ell(w)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)$. By inversion ($w\mapsto w^{-1}$ preserves lengths and interchanges the two coset families $\{W_Ja\}$ and $\{aW_J\}$), every left coset $aW_J:=\{au:u\in W_J\}$ has a unique minimal element $d$, characterized by $\ell(ds)>\ell(d)$ for all $s\in J$ and satisfying $\ell(du)=\ell(d)+\ell(u)$ for all $u\in W_J$.
4. **Type A.** Let $n\ge2$, $S=\{s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}\}$ and $m(s_i,s_j):=3$ if $|i-j|=1$, $m(s_i,s_j):=2$ if $|i-j|>1$ (a Coxeter matrix of type $A_{n-1}$). Then $s_i\mapsto(i\ i+1)$ extends to an isomorphism $W\to S_n$ (the letters $1,\dots,n$ carry the library's symmetric group by the order-preserving identification with $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$, under which $(i\ i+1)$ is the adjacent transposition $(i-1\ i)$), and for every $w\in W$,
$$\ell(w)=\operatorname{inv}\bigl(\varphi(w)\bigr),$$
the inversion number of the corresponding permutation ([[def-inversions-inversion-number-and-sign]]). In particular a word in the $s_i$ is reduced if and only if its length equals the inversion number of its value.

Since $L_j=X_j$ by [[lem-hh-cyclotomic-commuting-jucys-murphy-generators]], it fixes every $L_j$. Its restriction to the finite type-A Hecke subalgebra is the reversal anti-involution.

Let $R$, $v_s$, $H$, $T_s$ be as in [[def-hh-universal-coxeter-hecke-parameters-and-presentation]], let $(S,m)$, $W$, $\ell$ be as in [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]], and let $\{T_w:w\in W\}$ be the standard basis of $H$ ([[thm-hh-generic-coxeter-hecke-standard-basis]]).

2. **Invertibility.** Each generator is a unit: $T_s^{-1}=T_s-(v_s-v_s^{-1})$, and each $T_w=T_{s_1}\cdots T_{s_k}$ is a unit with $T_w^{-1}=T_{s_k}^{-1}\cdots T_{s_1}^{-1}$.

and $T_s=v_s^{-1}S_s$. If $v_s=v$ for all $s\in S$ (one odd component) and $Q:=v^2$, both relations read $(S_s-Q)(S_s+1)=0$ for every $s$. Fix $r,n\ge1$ and work in the universal cyclotomic algebra $H_{r,n}$ of [[def-hh-multiplicative-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]], with parameters $Q,u_1,\ldots,u_r$, commuting Jucys–Murphy generators $L_i=X_i$, and finite generators $T_i$. For an $r$-multipartition $\lambda$, put $a_c=\sum_{d<c}|\lambda^{(d)}|$ and define
$$u_\lambda=\prod_{c=2}^{r}\ \prod_{i=1}^{a_c}(L_i-u_c).$$
Let $t^\lambda$ be the row-standard initial multitableau from [[def-hh-cell-datum-dominance-and-cell-ideals]]. Let $S_\lambda$ be the subgroup of $S_n$ that permutes labels within each row of $t^\lambda$, and set $x_\lambda=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$ and $m_\lambda=u_\lambda x_\lambda$. The anti-involution $*$ is the generator-fixing map of [[lem-hh-cyclotomic-anti-involution-fixes-generators]].

For a standard multitableau $t$, use the right entry action $t\cdot w:=w^{-1}\cdot t$, where the left action applies $w$ to every entry. Let $d(t)$ be the unique permutation with $t^\lambda\cdot d(t)=t$. Standardness implies that $d(t)$ is the distinguished minimal representative for its row-stabilizer coset. For standard $s,t$ of shape $\lambda$, define
$$m_{st}=T_{d(s)}^*m_\lambda T_{d(t)}.$$
These are specified elements of $H_{r,n}$; this definition does not assert their linear independence or cellularity.

Fix $r,n\ge1$ and use the independent units $Q,u_1,\ldots,u_r$ of [[def-hh-multiplicative-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]. An **$r$-multipartition** of $n$ is a tuple $\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(r)})$ of ordinary partitions whose total number of boxes is $n$. Its boxes are triples $(c,a,b)$ with $1\le c\le r$, $a\ge1$, and $1\le b\le\lambda^{(c)}_a$. Order the boxes within component $c$ by the transitive closure of $(c,a,b)<(c,a,b+1)$ and $(c,a,b)<(c,a+1,b)$; boxes in different components are incomparable.

A **standard multitableau** $t$ of shape $\lambda$ is a bijective filling of the boxes by $1,\ldots,n$ that increases along every row and column. Equivalently, it is a linear extension of this finite box poset. Write $\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)$ for the set of such fillings and

$$ \operatorname{res}_t(i)=u_cQ^{b-a}\quad\text{if entry }i\text{ occupies }(c,a,b). $$

The **generic content field** is $K=\mathbb Q(Q,u_1,\ldots,u_r)$, the fraction field of $R$. The contents of distinct addable boxes of any multipartition are distinct in $K$. If two boxes in one component have the same content, they lie on one diagonal; the right and lower boxes immediately between them are distinct required predecessors of the southeast box. Consequently, for three consecutive labels $i,i+1,i+2$ in a standard multitableau, the first and third contents cannot agree. In particular every pair of contents among three consecutive labels is distinct in $K$. If two boxes in one component have content exponents differing by $1$, then they are comparable in the box order, so interchanging adjacent labels in a standard multitableau never gives a content ratio $Q$ or $Q^{-1}$.

Let $R_A=\mathbb Z[Q^{\pm1}]$ and let $H_n$ be the type-A Hecke algebra on $T_1,\ldots,T_{n-1}$ with braid relations and $(T_i-Q)(T_i+1)=0$. For a partition $\lambda\vdash n$, let $t^\lambda$ be row-filled, $S_\lambda$ its row subgroup, $x_\lambda=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$, and
$$m_{st}=T_{d(s)}^*x_\lambda T_{d(t)}$$
for standard $\lambda$-tableaux, with the tableau action and distinguished representatives fixed in [[def-hh-cyclotomic-murphy-elements]]. Then the $m_{st}$ form an $R_A$-basis of $H_n$, $m_{st}^*=m_{ts}$, and the spans $H_n^{\trianglerighteq\lambda}$ and $H_n^{\triangleright\lambda}$ of shapes respectively dominating and strictly dominating $\lambda$ are two-sided ideals. For every $h\in H_n$ and standard $s,t$ of shape $\lambda$,
$$m_{st}h\equiv\sum_{v\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)}r_{t,v}(h)m_{sv}\pmod{H_n^{\triangleright\lambda}},$$
where $r_{t,v}(h)\in R_A$ does not depend on $s$. The proof is integral over $R_A$; it does not divide by $Q+1$ or assume semisimplicity.

Let $A=\mathbb Z[Q,Q^{-1}]$ and let $H_{n,A}$ have braid relations and $(T_i-Q)(T_i+1)=0$. For a composition $\alpha$ of $n$, let $x_\alpha=\sum_{w\in S_\alpha}T_w$ and let $s,t$ be row-standard $\alpha$-tableaux. Define $m^\alpha_{st}=T_{d(s)}^*x_\alpha T_{d(t)}$ using [[def-hh-cyclotomic-murphy-elements]]. For row-standard tableaux of possibly different shapes, write $u\unrhd_{\rm tab}s$ when, for every label cutoff $m$ and row cutoff $j$, the number of entries at most $m$ in the first $j$ rows of $u$ is at least the corresponding number for $s$. In the unique standard-Murphy expansion
$$m^\alpha_{st}=\sum_{\mu\vdash n}\ \sum_{u,v\in\operatorname{Std}(\mu)}c_{uv}m^\mu_{uv},$$
each nonzero coefficient satisfies $u\unrhd_{\rm tab}s$, $v\unrhd_{\rm tab}t$, and $\mu\unrhd\bar\alpha$, where $\bar\alpha$ is the partition obtained by sorting the parts of $\alpha$. These are integral identities over $A$, and they specialize to every commutative ring with a unit Hecke parameter. Generic semisimplicity is used to prove coordinate vanishing over $A$; semisimplicity is not assumed after specialization.

Let $(S,m)$ be a finite Coxeter matrix with presented group $W$, length $\ell$ and geometric representation $\sigma:W\to\mathrm{GL}_K(E)$ as in [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]], [[def-hh-geometric-coxeter-representation-and-roots]] and [[lem-hh-dihedral-root-recurrence-and-root-sign]], and let $J\subseteq S$.

1. **Support and reduction.** For every $w\in W$ the set $S(w)$ of letters occurring in a reduced expression of $w$ is independent of the reduced expression, and every word in $S$ representing $w$ can be transformed into a reduced expression by repeatedly deleting two letters (Tits reduction, using only letters already present). Consequently
$$W_J=\langle J\rangle=\{w\in W:S(w)\subseteq J\}.$$
2. **Intrinsic parabolic presentation.** Let $W_J^\ast$ be the group presented by the restricted Coxeter matrix $(J,m|_J)$ in the sense of [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]. The canonical homomorphism $W_J^\ast\to W_J$, $s\mapsto s$, is an isomorphism. Hence $(W_J,J)$ is a Coxeter system, its intrinsic length function $\ell_J$ agrees with the ambient length $\ell$ on $W_J$, and $W_J\cap S=J$.
3. **Minimal coset representatives.** Every right coset $W_J a:=\{ua:u\in W_J\}$ ($a\in W$, [[def-coset]]) has a unique element $d$ of minimal length; it is characterized by $\ell(sd)>\ell(d)$ for all $s\in J$, and it satisfies
$$\ell(ud)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)\qquad\text{for all }u\in W_J .$$
Equivalently, every $w\in W$ has a unique factorization $w=u\,d$ with $u\in W_J$ and $d$ the minimal representative of the right coset $W_J d$, and then $\ell(w)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)$. By inversion ($w\mapsto w^{-1}$ preserves lengths and interchanges the two coset families $\{W_Ja\}$ and $\{aW_J\}$), every left coset $aW_J:=\{au:u\in W_J\}$ has a unique minimal element $d$, characterized by $\ell(ds)>\ell(d)$ for all $s\in J$ and satisfying $\ell(du)=\ell(d)+\ell(u)$ for all $u\in W_J$.
4. **Type A.** Let $n\ge2$, $S=\{s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}\}$ and $m(s_i,s_j):=3$ if $|i-j|=1$, $m(s_i,s_j):=2$ if $|i-j|>1$ (a Coxeter matrix of type $A_{n-1}$). Then $s_i\mapsto(i\ i+1)$ extends to an isomorphism $W\to S_n$ (the letters $1,\dots,n$ carry the library's symmetric group by the order-preserving identification with $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$, under which $(i\ i+1)$ is the adjacent transposition $(i-1\ i)$), and for every $w\in W$,
$$\ell(w)=\operatorname{inv}\bigl(\varphi(w)\bigr),$$
the inversion number of the corresponding permutation ([[def-inversions-inversion-number-and-sign]]). In particular a word in the $s_i$ is reduced if and only if its length equals the inversion number of its value.

Let $R_A=\mathbb Z[Q^{\pm1}]$ and let $H_n$ be the type-A Hecke algebra on $T_1,\ldots,T_{n-1}$ with braid relations and $(T_i-Q)(T_i+1)=0$. For a partition $\lambda\vdash n$, let $t^\lambda$ be row-filled, $S_\lambda$ its row subgroup, $x_\lambda=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$, and
$$m_{st}=T_{d(s)}^*x_\lambda T_{d(t)}$$
for standard $\lambda$-tableaux, with the tableau action and distinguished representatives fixed in [[def-hh-cyclotomic-murphy-elements]]. Then the $m_{st}$ form an $R_A$-basis of $H_n$, $m_{st}^*=m_{ts}$, and the spans $H_n^{\trianglerighteq\lambda}$ and $H_n^{\triangleright\lambda}$ of shapes respectively dominating and strictly dominating $\lambda$ are two-sided ideals. For every $h\in H_n$ and standard $s,t$ of shape $\lambda$,
$$m_{st}h\equiv\sum_{v\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)}r_{t,v}(h)m_{sv}\pmod{H_n^{\triangleright\lambda}},$$
where $r_{t,v}(h)\in R_A$ does not depend on $s$. The proof is integral over $R_A$; it does not divide by $Q+1$ or assume semisimplicity.

$$ L_1=X_1,\qquad L_i=Q^{1-i}T_{i-1}\cdots T_1X_1T_1\cdots T_{i-1}\quad(2\le i\le n). $$

Then $L_i=X_i$ for every $i$, so the $L_i$ commute and are units. For $1\le i<n$ they satisfy

$$ T_iL_iT_i=QL_{i+1},\qquad T_iL_i=L_{i+1}T_i-(Q-1)L_{i+1},\qquad T_iL_{i+1}=L_iT_i+(Q-1)L_{i+1}, $$

and $T_iL_j=L_jT_i$ when $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$. More generally, for every polynomial $f\in R[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$,

$$ T_if(L_1,\ldots,L_n)=f(s_iL_1,\ldots,s_iL_n)T_i-(Q-1)L_{i+1}\frac{f(L_1,\ldots,L_n)-f(s_iL_1,\ldots,s_iL_n)}{L_i-L_{i+1}}, $$

Let $B_r$ be the interval of labels occupying row $r$ of $t^\alpha$, and write $x_\alpha=\sum a_{uv}R_{uv}$. Fix a right index $v$ and an adjacent pair $i,i+1$ inside $B_r$. Choose a reduced expression $d(s)=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_k}$. Every reduced prefix is a distinguished row representative: write $d(s)=ab$ with $a$ that prefix and $\ell(d(s))=\ell(a)+\ell(b)$.
